title: My automated Claude-code trading
author: RickSmith3821
selftext:
For those that haven't seen my posts... I had Claude Code build me a futures trading system in python.  It has a browser tab extension that it uses to grab the real time quote information from my tradingview account, and then fires trades through [pickmytrade.trade](http://pickmytrade.trade) to a [tradovate.com](http://tradovate.com) sim account.  (closest thing you can find to real money / real rules / real slippage factors)

Started a demo account with $6k seed.  9 sessions in the bag, 1 in progress (today) and I'm net +4738 after commissions and fees.  I don't do ANYthing manually in this account - Claude's connected to me / the account through a Discord channel where I can type 'exit' and kill a trade if I want, etc.  Pretty cool.

Wins / losses;

Here’s your balance session by session, starting from $6,000 when the Oct 13 session opened (Oct 12, 6 PM):

|Session|Trades|Wins / losses|Gross P&L|Balance|
|:-|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Start||||$6,000|
|Oct 13|29|12 / 17|−$3,677|$2,323|
|Oct 14|15|8 / 7|\+$1,960|$4,283|
|Oct 15|24|11 / 13|\+$795|$5,078|
|Oct 16|18|9 / 9|\+$5,775|$10,853|
|Oct 19|17|11 / 6|\+$865|$11,718|
|Oct 20|17|10 / 7|\+$4,215|$15,933|
|Oct 21|44|18 / 25|−$1,782|$14,151|
|Oct 22|11|9 / 2|\+$19,375|$33,526|
|Oct 23|22|10 / 12|\+$840|$34,366|
|Oct 26|15|9 / 5|\+$699|$35,065|
|Oct 27 (so far)|6|2 / 4|\+$2,410|$37,475|

Total: 218 trades, 109 wins and 107 losses, +$31,475. That ends $137 above your actual $37,338, so the numbers line up.

* Lowest point: $2,323 after the first session, when the account was down $3,677, almost 61% of the $6,000.
* If the start is midnight Oct 13 instead, the total is +$33,065, which overshoots your balance by about $1,700. Counting from the 6 PM open fits your account much better.
* About fees: subtracting estimated commissions (about $3,000) would put you around $34,400, well below your actual balance. So it looks like this account isn’t being charged per-trade fees the way the scanner assumes.

The rest still holds: the NQ scanner made +$32,775, the separate MNQ trades lost $1,300, and the 4-contract doubled trades account for about $19.6K of the gain.  (on 10/22 we ran two scanners (since been outlawed programatically) and thank God it was a good day... haha. it doubled all the trades to 4 and 2 instead of 2 and 1 .. normally the system places 2 NQ trades, sells off one and lets one run or stop out... mostly profitable.)

  
More info in another week, but this is the most promising I've seen out of 6 months now of testing a ton of different strategies.

comments.author: wkerstens
comments.body: Is Claude also handling the actual strategy / opening / closing or is this still hardcoded into the python script?

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body: Nope.  All the logic is in the python.  The only thing Claude does is has access to my trading view account to be able to get real-time" information.  And that's done through a Chrome extension tab. So when the scanner starts it pops open a browser window you got to authorize it and then he has access to my tradingview account to do quoting.  But there's no AI interaction during the trading other than what it's written in Python. My plan is once I go live with real money it'll be through the trado API and the python scanner will have access to real-time quotes through that so that will simplify things.

replies.author: wkerstens
replies.body:
So only the initial "research" is done using Claude, daily, and then Python takes over?

It does simplify things I think, getting my python script to correctly record all relevant quotes took quite some effort.

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body: No.... Claude has permissions to the claude extension in a chrome browser.  So the python script calls through that to get real-time quotes.   But that's just a tunnel for the real time quotes...

replies.author: wkerstens
replies.body: Got it, thanks for your explanation.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Cool setup, and it's good that you let it run without stepping in. Two things I'd check. A lot of the gain seems to come from one big day, so it's worth seeing how the curve looks without it. Sim fills are also usually kinder than real ones, and if the account isn't charging commissions, live results would likely come in lower. If you want to keep testing agents without risking money, Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs them in paper mode on a practice balance.

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body: The "net" I list above is including commissions and fees for tradovate.   I have had Claude analyze slippage .. the demo accounts in tradovate are really close to the real numbers so I'm not worried there...   MOST of the wins come from that one day, yes, but even without that doubling, that was still an 11k day... sooo 👍

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for clearing that up, I got the commissions part wrong. That's a fair point on the one day, an 11k day even without the doubling is still a good day. I'd still look at how the rest of the sessions add up, since a few more weeks of normal days will say more about the edge.

comments.author: SPXQuantAlgo
comments.body: Why does everyone who posts this always use paper account? It is absolutely useless. Do it live, even a small account, and then share real results.

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body: It's not as useless as you think.  I've run the numbers ... tradovate fills are really close live / demo.  And my python system takes out commissions and fees as well... so "net" is "net".   And you use a paper account to get it 90% done, then take it live and see how it does in the real world.

replies.author: SPXQuantAlgo
replies.body: Exactly. As soon as it’s live post the results. Why do you think the only posts here are paper? Because it does NOT work live. But feel free to prove me wrong ofc I’d be happy.

replies.body: I keep reading this, but in my case (using IBKR) paper trading is worse than live so far. Could well be an IBKR issue, but it's slower, and fills worse. Live it's absolutely fine and slippage is not more than I accounted for.

replies.author: RickSmith3821

replies.author: real_PommesPanzer
replies.body: Well, you can trade paper only. When it works on paper it works in reality. You doing a simulated trade using money on real stock prices.

replies.author: SPXQuantAlgo
replies.body: No it doesn’t work in reality. In reality you get fucked by slippage, fees and commissions, queue priority etc

replies.author: real_PommesPanzer
replies.body: Everything is know. Fees as best example are well known before trading some broker take percentage some fixed amount.

replies.author: scp-8989
replies.body: I second this. The paper trading is not the same as real trading to humans because of the psychology thing. But to machine it is (almost) identical.

replies.author: alrachid
replies.body: No, it’s not true that if it works on paper it works with real money. The paper bot cannot assume fills on fast moving prices and trades. Sure, on paper a low frequency bot should be fairly accurate, but not higher frequency trading and scalping.

replies.author: RNAlgotrading
replies.body: You are absolutely wrong. Paper trading can give you a confident that your algo is strong and making money, You can keep those results with you, no one will ask, But when you post those numbers on a public, you need to post the real numbers. How many years are you in trading? Have you done trading with real money. Trading is where 80% psychological and 20% logical. when you do paper trading, you are doing 100% logical, but with real money, it is difficult, that's what everyone is trying to teach you here.

replies.author: real_PommesPanzer
replies.body:
Depends on what you want to do. It all depends on your data sources.

Orders can always be transmitted via API some broker allow that. 

In my case, I have a special test api to verify. It has the same functionality but do not deduct you funds. It simulate trades exactly how it should behave in reality. The broker allows that especially for testing 

Every other assumption you do is entirely by your implementation. Do you gather information regularly, do you search for news outlets, how do get you analysis data.

Technically you could build your own Bloombergterminal with ai decision
